skill.name: qa-check
skill.description: Runs pre-PR quality checks for a Gradle backend and pnpm frontend. It verifies lint, tests, builds, and coverage before reporting pass or fail.
skill.summary: Checks backend and frontend quality gates before a pull request.
skill.author: Crearize

security_audit.summary: The skill intentionally guides an agent to run local Gradle, pnpm, cd, ls, pwd, and chmod commands for QA checks. Several static matches are Markdown formatting or path references and were dismissed as false positives. No evidence found for prompt injection, network exfiltration, or obfuscated payloads.

remediation.issue: Local command execution during QA checks
remediation.suggestion: Require explicit user confirmation before running Gradle, pnpm, cd, chmod, or other shell commands.

remediation.issue: Repository scripts may execute project code
remediation.suggestion: Warn users to run this skill only in trusted repositories and to review package and Gradle scripts first.
Replace the personal path with a user-provided project root or a relative workspace check.
Ask for approval before changing executable bits and explain why the permission change is needed.

content.user_title: Run QA Checks Before Pull Requests
content.value_statement: Teams need consistent checks before opening pull requests. This skill guides lint, test, build, and coverage validation for frontend and backend work.
actual_capabilities: Verifies project location and expected Gradle or frontend files before running checks.
Runs backend Gradle checks and optional JaCoCo coverage verification.
Runs frontend lint, build, and coverage commands for the frontend package.
Applies pass, fail, and warning criteria to QA results.
Produces a Markdown QA report with summaries, details, and next steps.
limitations: Assumes a Gradle backend and a pnpm frontend package layout.
Requires project dependencies and scripts to already exist locally.
Uses fixed coverage thresholds from the skill instructions.
Reports failures but does not automatically repair failing code.

use_cases.title: Pre-merge Quality Gate
use_cases.description: Validate backend and frontend checks before requesting review.

use_cases.title: Frontend Regression Check
use_cases.description: Run lint, build, tests, and coverage after UI changes.

use_cases.title: Release Readiness Review
use_cases.description: Create a structured QA report for release approval.

prompt_templates.title: Run Full QA
prompt_templates.prompt: Use qa-check to validate both backend and frontend before I open a pull request.

prompt_templates.title: Check Frontend Only
prompt_templates.prompt: Use qa-check with target frontend and report lint, build, test, and coverage results.

prompt_templates.title: Check Backend Without Coverage
prompt_templates.prompt: Use qa-check with target backend and skip coverage because I need a fast verification pass.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare Release Gate Report
prompt_templates.prompt: Use qa-check for both targets. Include command outcomes, coverage gaps, failing tests, and exact next actions for release readiness.

output_examples.input: Run a full QA check before a pull request.
output: Overall result: failed because frontend coverage is below threshold.
Backend checks passed. Frontend lint and build passed. Coverage needs improvement before review.

output_examples.input: Check frontend only after a UI change.
output_examples.output: Frontend result: passed. Lint, build, tests, and coverage completed successfully.
Backend result: warning. Gradle checks passed, but coverage was skipped and should be verified before merge.

best_practices: Run the skill from the project root after dependencies are installed.
Review each command before execution in unfamiliar repositories.
Use coverage skipping only for quick checks, not final merge approval.
anti_patterns: Do not run repository scripts from untrusted code without review.
Do not treat skipped coverage as release-ready evidence.
Do not ignore failed commands when preparing a pull request.

faq.question: Does this skill run commands?
faq.answer: Yes. It guides the agent to run local Gradle and pnpm commands in the workspace.

faq.question: Can I use it outside MovieMarketer?
faq.answer: Yes, if your repository has a compatible Gradle backend and pnpm frontend layout.

faq.question: Does it install dependencies?
faq.answer: No. Install project dependencies before running the checks.

faq.question: Can coverage checks be skipped?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill supports a skip coverage option for faster checks.

faq.question: Does it fix failing tests?
faq.answer: No. It reports failures and suggests next steps.

faq.question: Is it safe for untrusted repositories?
faq.answer: Use caution. Build and package scripts can execute code from the repository.
